label: ex:li6-derived-nf
title: Li-6: post-magic operator transition
html:
Example. Lithium-6 (Z = 3, N = 3, A = 6) is the lightest nucleus beyond the doubly-magic helium-4 core. Its construction demonstrates the operator transition from Regime II (Hopf link) back to Regime III (bare crossing) after the He-4 magic shell closes.

Inductive construction

The He-4 core is built by Regime I \to II operators. The fifth nucleon still uses a Hopf link, riding the stability of the doubly-magic core. But the sixth nucleon transitions to the bare mixed crossing C_{pn} (Regime III).

Normal form at q_0

  \mathrm{NF}(\mathcal{A}(3,3))
  \approx
  +0.087\gamma + 0.130\sigma_0 + 0.455\sigma_1 + 0.205 L_+ + 1.288 L_- + 0.589 e^-
  \mathrm{net} \approx +2.754, \qquad
  |\mathrm{def}| = 0
  \quad \text{(all coefficients positive).}

Physical interpretation

  1. All coefficients are positive. Li-6 is deficit-free. This is consistent with Li-6 being the lightest stable lithium isotope.
  2. The dominant term is L_-. This reflects the strong neutron-proton Hopf binding inherited from the He-4 core.
  3. The operator transition at step 6 marks the passage from the magic-shell regime to the open-shell regime. Beyond this point, nucleons interact via bare crossings. The collective shell effect diminishes.
  4. The e^- coefficient is positive. The nucleus absorbs the trefoil deficit. The positive e^- means the nucleus is a trefoil supplier, not a deficit-bearer. It can emit electrons without beta-decay instability.
